do unto others as you would have them do unto you phrase

also do as you would be done by, the golden rule

classical

Publil. Sent. A 2
Sen. Ep. 94.43: ab aliō expectēs alterī quod fēceris

Ab aliō expectēs, alterī quod fēceris.

Literally “you may expect from another what you have done to another”: a line of Publilius Syrus, which Seneca quotes as a saying that needs no proof. It speaks of what comes back to you rather than of a duty, as the English does.

Other words

  • Ab aliō exspectēs alterī quod fēceris.

    also used · modern · Traupman 255
